### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **85** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**54** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad155795766d51cb8c3105bb688c6ba0f3554e32`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **11** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 56 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad155795766d51cb8c3105bb688c6ba0f3554e32` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `19f003cc25576258fc8ad29a23935787da4eccb8` — the merge of head `3f9f00da9a9f9649d643204f87d50880d4037530` into base `ad155795766d51cb8c3105bb688c6ba0f3554e32`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 19f003cc25576258fc8ad29a23935787da4eccb8 && git checkout 19f003cc25576258fc8ad29a23935787da4eccb8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ad155795766d51cb8c3105bb688c6ba0f3554e32 3f9f00da9a9f9649d643204f87d50880d4037530 && git checkout -B drift-repro ad155795766d51cb8c3105bb688c6ba0f3554e32 && git merge --no-ff 3f9f00da9a9f9649d643204f87d50880d4037530

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ad155795766d51cb8c3105bb688c6ba0f3554e32
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ad155795766d51cb8c3105bb688c6ba0f3554e32` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a27aab1edff015f2b8659a2feb04ffcaea67af06`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/ai-answer.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + packages/spec/src/api/ai-answer.test.ts, packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/variant-docs.json, packages/spec/llms.txt, packages/spec/api-surface/api.json, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json

Brief: 6987021550 with delta 6987302827. Read: card #32642, claim 6983810316, amendment 6986582518, os-dev reports 6986537715 and 6986993915, the PR body, the full diff against merge-base `ec227fc7b1`, the changeset, the head's check-runs, and the producer at cloud `c21b372` (read only). Code outside the diff that was read, not reviewed: `packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/refinement-projection.ts`.

Three findings: one must-fix (F1), one should-fix (F2), one nit (F3).

### ① Derived judgments

CI on this head is not complete. Finished and green: Check Changeset (the later run 135020754956; the earlier run 135018011211 on this head is the PR-body line, since fixed), Lint (all lanes), Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check source gates and debt ledger, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Build Docs. Still running when read: Build Core, Type Check workspace and consumer gates, Test Core 1 to 10, the UI lanes. The head differs from `a9d47c0f21` by two changeset lines only; on `a9d47c0f21` Build Core, Type Check source gates and consumer gates were green and the Test Core shards that finished were green (the rest were cancelled by the push). The judgments below rest on the diff and the producer, not on the unfinished runs.

Against the producer, field by field:

- Saved question (`AiSavedQuestionSchema`): seven members, types and nullability equal `SavedQuestion` at `saved-question-store.ts:80-88`, built by `toSaved` at 114-124. `source` reuses `ObjectQuerySourceSchema`, the schema the producer itself parses the stored block with (`source-artifact.ts:109-111`). Holds.
- List: `questions`, newest first, limit 200 (`saved-question-routes.ts:274`, store 218-224). Holds.
- Create request: the four keys the handler reads (294-296, 308); `source` in a body is not read (292). `dependentRequired` in both directions equals the pair rule at 297; `requiredOneOf` is at-least-one (`refinement-projection.ts:281-290`), so a body with both a question and a turn parses, as the producer accepts it (311). Holds.
- Create response 201 `question`; DELETE 204 or 404; run response `question`, `toolName`, `result` (330, 348-349, 394); `toolName` union at `source-artifact.ts:186`. Holds.
- Artifact request `kind`, `toolCallId`, `label` (413-432, kinds at `source-artifact.ts:49`). Response by `kind`: the view arm `id` optional, `object_name`, `label`, `config` (451-452, `source-artifact.ts:504-508`); report and widget arms `published: false`, two drafts, `dataset`, and `report` or `dashboard` (474-483). Holds.
- Feedback: stored shape equals `AnswerFeedback` (`answer-feedback-store.ts:82-89`); GET answers null when unrated (`feedback-routes.ts:132`); POST `rating` required, `note` string, null or absent (148-164); DELETE 204 and idempotent (185-187). Holds.
- Refusal reasons: the two saved-question reasons (371, 392) and the eleven artifact reasons (35-37, 428, `source-artifact.ts:53-69`) are complete; `details.question` and `details.issues` match (371, 86). Holds.
- Error codes, measured against the handlers only: each of the three lists is exactly what the handler's `sendError` calls emit. Measured against the wire, they are not closed: see F1.
- Required against optional, and refinements: nothing the producer always sends is optional and nothing it may omit is required. The two refinements are declared through the closed list, so they project.
- Length caps (2000, 500) in `.describe()` only: correct. The producer trims before it measures (296 and 318; `feedback-routes.ts:160-161`), so a schema `max` would refuse bodies the server accepts.
- `turnId` on the conversation message, wire and contract: optional on both; the CONTROL test parses a stored conversation without it; the `AIConversation` contract change is a widening for implementers (a service returning plain `ModelMessage` items still satisfies it). One reservation: F2.
- Naming: verb-first request and response names (`ListAi…`, `CreateAi…`, `SetAi…`) match the siblings `ListAiConversationsResponseSchema`, `CreateAiConversationRequestSchema`, `ListAiPendingActionsResponseSchema` in `protocol.zod.ts`. camelCase keys match the conversation wire object; `object_name` in the view arm is the producer's own row key.
- Exports: `@objectstack/spec/api` gains 22 schemas and 22 types from `ai-answer.zod.ts` plus `AiConversationMessageSchema` and `AiConversationMessage` (46 lines added to `api-surface/api.json`, none removed); `@objectstack/spec/contracts` gains `AIConversationMessage`. Nothing is removed or renamed.
- Generated artefacts: the surface, declaration-map, export-origins, manifest and reference-docs changes are additions that follow the source; `check:generated` runs in Build Core, still running on this head and green on `a9d47c0f21` with the same source. The hand-kept ledgers (`dropped-refinements.baseline.json` three rows, all the inherited `source.filter` site of `ObjectQuerySourceSchema`; `variant-docs.json` one not-authorable row; `llms.txt` counts; 23 isomorphic pins) each state what the diff adds.

**F1 (must-fix). The three error vocabularies are declared closed, and they are not the codes these paths answer.** The file header says every failure body carries an `error` that is one of the three route errors, and each `…ErrorCodeSchema` is documented as the `error.code` vocabulary of its routes. Both mount paths in this repo refuse an anonymous caller of an `auth: true` AI route before the handler runs, with `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` (`domains/ai.ts:63-67` and the per-route gate after it; `dispatcher-plugin.ts:290-301`; `ANONYMOUS_DENY_CODE` in `anonymous-deny.ts:74`). The same door answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` on every one of these paths when no AI service is serveable, `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` before the route table is published, and `405` for an undeclared method. None of the three lists holds `UNAUTHENTICATED`; the saved-question and feedback lists hold neither `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` nor `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. So the commonest failure a console meets, an expired session, does not parse against `AiSavedQuestionErrorSchema`, `AiAnswerArtifactErrorSchema` or `AiAnswerFeedbackErrorSchema`, and a consumer that switches exhaustively on the published code type has no arm for it. The handler's own `401 PERMISSION_DENIED` (cited at `saved-question-routes.ts:156`, `feedback-routes.ts:96`) is reached only where the deployment does not require authentication. The same holds for `details`: once present it must carry `reason`, which a door-level error does not. This has to be right before release, because adding a member to a published response-code enum later breaks exhaustive consumers. Either fix is acceptable: (a) add the door's codes to each list, at least `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, with a test that parses the door's 401 body; or (b) keep the lists as the handler's own vocabulary and say so in the header, the three `…ErrorCodeSchema` docs and the changeset: a failure on these paths is `ApiErrorSchema` first, and the route error schema applies only to a refusal the route handler itself answers. The changeset sentence on Errors and the generated `ai-answer.mdx` follow whichever is chosen.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset, and they agree. `@objectstack/spec` is graded `minor`.

- `added` with `minor` is the correct grade. `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains 62 keys, and the level gate refuses `none` on a PR that moves that shard. These are wire shapes that nobody writes into metadata, so by the prose rule alone the change would read as `none`; the shard counts request and response keys all the same, and `added` at `minor` is the declaration the gate admits. It errs on the safe side: it over-states the level, never under-states it, and it is not `major`.
- `yes (widening)`: new exports and one optional key. Nothing exported is removed, renamed or made required. The one place the accept set tightens is F2.
- Changeset prose against the diff: the route list, schema names, the `kind` values, the 201 and 204 statuses and the `turnId` paragraph all match the source. The Errors bullet repeats the closed-vocabulary claim of F1 and moves with its fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, location in `packages/spec/src/api/` not `src/ai/`: accepted in 6986582518 and right; every sibling wire shape lives in `api/protocol.zod.ts`.
- Dev deviation, `turnId` on the contract and the wire schema, `src/ai/conversation.zod.ts` untouched: right; that file is the memory-protocol shape.
- Dev deviation, first-round `Metadata-protocol: none` at `patch`: superseded by the delta 6987302827; judged in ②.
- Not declared, `GET /api/v1/ai/feedback/eval-cases`: accepted in 6986582518. The producer's own route ledger marks it `server-only` (`ai-route-ledger.ts:263`), which supports leaving it out.
- Caps described, not enforced: accepted in 6986582518 and correct (see ①).
- `check:generated` heap flake and the regenerated `authorable-surface/api.json` in round 2: no hand edit is visible in the diff; the file's change is additions in sorted order.
- Round 2 pushed before its overlap check: process only, no effect on the diff.
- NOT MEASURED, six gates that need another workspace package built: CI owns them. The Lint lanes are green on this head; Build Core is still running. Not a finding; the seat reads the finished runs before landing.
- Open question 1, spelling: answered `turnId` in 6986582518, applied in `4f312a82e7`. The PR body now spells it `turnId` throughout.
- Open question 2, cloud confirmation (card acceptance item 3): answered in 6986582518, deferred to the cloud lane, carried by #31865. Two cloud-side facts for that follow-up, neither a change to this PR: the message mapper emits no turn id today (`objectql-conversation-service.ts:774-809`), and the cloud route ledger still lists the feedback routes as `gap` (`ai-route-ledger.ts:257-261`).
- Overlap with draft #35239: generated files only (`content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`, `content/docs/references/index.mdx`, the strictness counts page). Whichever lands second regenerates. The branch is 3 commits behind `main`.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no separate author to name. The PR is still a draft.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds schemas and types only; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/spec/src/api/ai-answer.zod.ts`: the success shapes hold against the producer and against the first consumers named on the card (client SDK #32644, console #31889 and #31865). Typing the artifact item bodies as records is the right call: embedding `DatasetSchema`, `ReportSchema`, `DashboardSchema` or `ListViewSchema` would apply their defaults on a client parse. The error shapes do not hold for the first consumer: F1.
- `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`: **F2 (should-fix). `turnId` refuses null, and the stored column is nullable.** `AiMessageSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so before this PR a message carrying `turnId` with any value parsed. `AiConversationMessageSchema` now types it `z.string().optional()`, so `turnId: null` is refused. No producer emits the key today, so nothing shipping breaks. The column it will be read from is `turn_id?: string | null` (`objectql-conversation-service.ts:91`), and the same producer maps null columns to null everywhere else in this PR's shapes (`AiSavedQuestion.turnId` is nullable; `text(row.turn_id)` at `saved-question-store.ts:121`). A cloud mapper written in that house style would emit null for every message stored with no turn, and the reloaded conversation would fail to parse. Decide it now, because admitting null after release changes the type readers hold: either accept `string | null | undefined` on the wire schema and the contract type, or keep absent-only and state in both docs and in the note owed to the cloud lane that the mapper must omit the key, never send null. This is also the one place where `(widening)` is not strictly true, which the changeset should say in a clause if absent-only is kept.
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`: holds. An intersection with an optional key keeps every existing implementer and reader compiling; the jsdoc link to `IAIConversationService.addMessage` names a real `turnId` parameter.
- `packages/spec/src/api/index.ts`: holds; one barrel line, and the source type-check gates are green.
- Implementing files: `ai-answer.test.ts` pins each producer body and each refusal named in ① and has the CONTROL; it has no case for a door-level failure body, which is how F1 went unseen. The pin test and ledgers agree with the source.
- **F3 (nit).** The header says a conversation that is not the caller's answers 403 on the artifact and feedback routes. Saving a question from an answer answers the same 403 (`ownTurn`, `saved-question-routes.ts:199-203`, reached from 306). Prose only; `PERMISSION_DENIED` is already in that list.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32642-ai-answer-routes-spec`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbYRqkDAGuse5Wqbohi`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3f9f00da9a9f9649d643204f87d50880d4037530`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/ai-answer.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/index.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + packages/spec/src/api/ai-answer.test.ts, packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/variant-docs.json, packages/spec/llms.txt, packages/spec/api-surface/api.json, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json

Re-review of the delta from `a27aab1edf` (record 6987445765, FAIL) to this head, round 4. Read: the area decisions 6987461764, the os-dev round-4 report 6988247410, the PR body as rewritten at 18:50Z, the diff between the two heads, and the head's check-runs. The delta holds a merge of `origin/main` (`4548c6395c`); this PR's own changes are the three commits after it, and only those are judged. Against `main` the PR still changes the same 23 files. Everything record 6987445765 found to hold is unchanged and still holds. Code outside the diff that was read, not reviewed: `packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts`.

F1 closed. F2 closed. F3 closed. One new nit, N1. No must-fix and no should-fix is open.

### ① Derived judgments

CI on this head is not complete. Finished and green: Check Changeset (one run; a second run is still in progress), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Lint scoped tooling self-tests. Still running when read: Build Core, all four Type Check lanes, the other Lint lanes, Test Core 1 to 10, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI. Nothing on this head has finished red. The judgments below rest on the diff; the seat reads the finished runs before landing.

- **F1, closed.** `UNAUTHENTICATED` is in all three code lists. `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` are in every list that lacked them (saved question: both; artifact: `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; feedback: both). I checked the door's bodies against the schemas, not only the codes: the anonymous refusal is written through `buildApiError`, which promotes `details.code` into `code` and leaves no `details` (`error-envelope.ts`, `splitSemanticCode`), so the body is `code`, `message`, `httpStatus` and parses against the saved-question and artifact errors, whose `details` requires `reason` once present. The 501 and the 503 carry a status-derived code and no `details`. The new test parses those three bodies against each of the three route errors, with a control that an off-list code is still refused; the dev reports one ablation per list (A20 to A22), each red. The file header, the three code docs and the changeset Errors bullet now say what the lists hold. The header also states, correctly, that a route mounted on the HTTP server answers the flat anonymous-deny body, which is not the envelope these schemas describe.
- **F2, closed.** `turnId` is `z.string().nullable().optional()` on `AiConversationMessageSchema` and `turnId?: string | null` on `AIConversationMessage`. Both docs say absent or null. A test parses a conversation whose messages carry `turnId: null`; ablation A23 is reported red. The key now accepts everything a mapper of the nullable column can emit.
- **F3, closed.** The header's 403 sentence names saving a question from an answer beside the artifact and feedback routes.
- Generated artefacts: `content/docs/references/api/ai-answer.mdx` and `protocol.mdx` changed, and each changed line follows the source change (the three enum lists, the header text, `string | null`). `authorable-surface/api.json` and the api-surface files did not move in this delta, which is right: no key or export was added. `check:generated` is reported green by the dev and runs in Build Core, still running.
- Exports: unchanged from the previous head. Nothing removed, renamed or narrowed.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset and agree; `@objectstack/spec` stays `minor`. The grade holds for the reasons in record 6987445765. With F2 fixed, the one place the accept set tightened against the passthrough base is gone for null; what remains refused on `turnId` is a non-string, non-null value, which no producer emits and no column can hold, so `(widening)` is a fair statement of the change. The changeset's Errors bullet and `turnId` paragraph match the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags
